formulas.title: Area of a Rectangle
formulas.meaning: The space enclosed by a rectangle with length l and width w.
formulas.explanation: Multiply the length by the width to find the space inside the rectangle.
formulas.example: A rectangle has length 8 cm and width 5 cm. A = 8 × 5 = 40 cm².

formulas.title: Area of a Triangle
formulas.meaning: The space enclosed by a triangle with base b and perpendicular height h.
formulas.explanation: Multiply the base by the height, then halve the result.
formulas.example: A triangle has base 10 cm and height 6 cm. A = ½ × 10 × 6 = 30 cm².

formulas.title: Area of a Parallelogram
formulas.meaning: The space enclosed by a parallelogram with base b and perpendicular height h.
formulas.explanation: Multiply the base by the perpendicular height between the two parallel sides.
formulas.example: A parallelogram has base 7 cm and height 4 cm. A = 7 × 4 = 28 cm².

formulas.title: Area of a Trapezium
formulas.meaning: The space enclosed by a trapezium with parallel sides a and b, and height h.

variables.meaning: Length of the other parallel side
Perpendicular height between the parallel sides

formulas.explanation: Add the two parallel sides, multiply by the height, then halve the result.
formulas.example: A trapezium has parallel sides 5 cm and 9 cm, height 4 cm. A = ½ × (5 + 9) × 4 = 28 cm².

formulas.title: Volume of a Cuboid
formulas.meaning: The space occupied by a cuboid with length l, width w, and height h.
formulas.explanation: Multiply length, width, and height together.
formulas.example: A cuboid measures 4 cm × 3 cm × 2 cm. V = 4 × 3 × 2 = 24 cm³.

formulas.title: Volume of a Cylinder
formulas.meaning: The space occupied by a cylinder with radius r and height h.
formulas.explanation: Find the area of the circular base (πr²), then multiply by the height.
formulas.example: A cylinder has radius 3 cm and height 10 cm. V = π × 3² × 10 ≈ 282.7 cm³.

formulas.title: Volume of a Sphere
formulas.meaning: The space occupied by a sphere with radius r.
formulas.explanation: Cube the radius, multiply by π, then multiply by 4/3.
formulas.example: A sphere has radius 6 cm. V = (4/3) × π × 6³ ≈ 904.8 cm³.

formulas.title: Volume of a Cone
formulas.meaning: The space occupied by a cone with base radius r and height h.
formulas.explanation: Find the volume of the equivalent cylinder (πr²h), then take a third of it.
formulas.example: A cone has radius 4 cm and height 9 cm. V = (1/3) × π × 4² × 9 ≈ 150.8 cm³.

formulas.title: Adding Fractions
formulas.meaning: Combines two fractions with different denominators into one.
formulas.explanation: Cross-multiply to get a common denominator, then add the numerators.

formulas.title: Multiplying Fractions
formulas.meaning: Combines two fractions by multiplying straight across.
formulas.explanation: Multiply the numerators together and the denominators together.

formulas.title: Dividing Fractions
formulas.meaning: Divides one fraction by another.
formulas.explanation: Flip (reciprocate) the second fraction, then multiply.

formulas.title: Percentage of an Amount
formulas.meaning: Finds what a given percentage of a total amount is.
formulas.explanation: Divide the percentage by 100 to get a decimal, then multiply by the amount.

formulas.title: Percentage Change
formulas.meaning: Measures how much a value has increased or decreased, as a percentage of the original.
formulas.explanation: Subtract the old value from the new value, divide by the old value, then multiply by 100.
formulas.example: A price rises from 40 to 50. Change % = ((50 − 40) / 40) × 100 = 25%.

formulas.title: Difference of Two Squares
formulas.meaning: Factorises the difference between two square terms.
formulas.explanation: Any expression in the form a² − b² can be factorised into (a + b)(a − b).

formulas.title: Perfect Square Expansion
formulas.meaning: Expands a squared bracket with two terms.
formulas.explanation: Square the first term, add double the product of both terms, then add the square of the second term.

formulas.title: Quadratic Formula
formulas.meaning: Solves any quadratic equation in the form ax² + bx + c = 0.
formulas.explanation: Substitute a, b, and c into the formula to find the two possible values of x.

formulas.title: Pythagoras' Theorem
formulas.meaning: Relates the three sides of a right-angled triangle.

variables.meaning: The hypotenuse (longest side, opposite the right angle)

formulas.explanation: The square of the hypotenuse equals the sum of the squares of the other two sides.
formulas.example: A right triangle has sides 3 cm and 4 cm. c² = 3² + 4² = 25, so c = 5 cm.

formulas.title: Circumference of a Circle
formulas.meaning: The distance around the outside of a circle.
formulas.explanation: Multiply the radius by 2, then multiply by π.
formulas.example: A circle has radius 5 cm. C = 2 × π × 5 ≈ 31.4 cm.

formulas.title: Area of a Circle
formulas.meaning: The space enclosed by a circle.
formulas.explanation: Square the radius, then multiply by π.
formulas.example: A circle has radius 4 cm. A = π × 4² ≈ 50.3 cm².

formulas.title: Arc Length
formulas.meaning: The length of a curved section of a circle's circumference.

variables.meaning: Angle of the arc in degrees

formulas.explanation: Find what fraction of the full circle the angle represents, then apply it to the circumference.
formulas.example: A 90° arc on a circle of radius 6 cm. L = (90/360) × 2π × 6 ≈ 9.4 cm.

formulas.title: SOHCAHTOA (Right-Angled Triangles)
formulas.formula: sin θ = O/H,  cos θ = A/H,  tan θ = O/A
formulas.meaning: Relates an angle in a right-angled triangle to the ratio of its sides.

variables.meaning: Adjacent side (next to the angle θ)

formulas.explanation: Choose the ratio (sin, cos, or tan) that matches the two sides you know or need to find.
formulas.example: A right triangle has hypotenuse 10 and angle 30°. Opposite = sin(30°) × 10 = 5.

formulas.title: Sine Rule
formulas.formula: a / sin A = b / sin B = c / sin C
formulas.meaning: Relates the sides and angles of any triangle (not just right-angled).
formulas.explanation: Use when you know a pair of opposite side/angle values plus one more side or angle.

formulas.title: Cosine Rule
formulas.meaning: Finds a missing side or angle in any triangle when the sine rule cannot be used directly.
formulas.explanation: Use when you know two sides and the angle between them, or all three sides.

formulas.title: Gradient of a Line
formulas.meaning: Measures how steep a straight line is between two points.
formulas.explanation: Divide the change in y (vertical) by the change in x (horizontal).

formulas.title: Distance Between Two Points
formulas.meaning: Finds the straight-line distance between two coordinates.
formulas.explanation: This is Pythagoras' theorem applied to the horizontal and vertical differences between the points.

formulas.title: Midpoint of a Line Segment
formulas.meaning: Finds the point exactly halfway between two coordinates.
formulas.explanation: Average the x-coordinates and average the y-coordinates.

formulas.title: Basic Probability
formulas.meaning: Measures how likely an event is to happen, from 0 (impossible) to 1 (certain).
formulas.explanation: Count the outcomes that satisfy the event, divide by the total number of possible outcomes.
formulas.example: Rolling a die: P(rolling an even number) = 3/6 = 1/2.

formulas.title: Combined Probability (AND, independent events)
formulas.meaning: Finds the probability of two independent events both happening.
formulas.explanation: Multiply the individual probabilities together, since the events don't affect each other.
formulas.example: P(heads on a coin) × P(rolling a 6) = 1/2 × 1/6 = 1/12.

formulas.title: Mean (Average)
formulas.meaning: The typical or central value of a data set.
formulas.explanation: Add up all the values, then divide by how many values there are.

formulas.title: Range
formulas.meaning: Measures how spread out a data set is.
formulas.explanation: Subtract the smallest value in the data set from the largest.
